title: Common refinements for already compactifiable morphisms over arbitrary schemes
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with separatedness and finite type as in [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], admitting at least one compactification, a factorization $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $p$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Consider the category of these compactifications with proper $Y$-maps $u:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ satisfying $uj_1=j_2$ as arrows [lem-nagata-refinements-form-category]. This category is cofiltered: every pair of objects has a common refinement, and every pair of parallel arrows is equalized by a refinement. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness assumption on $Y$ is made. For any $g:Y'\to Y$, base change sends objects and arrows to compactifications and refinements of $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$, preserves identities and compositions, and carries a common refinement or equalizer diagram to such a diagram. Base changes here are formed by fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: The compactifications and proper refinements form a category: identities and composites satisfy the defining equations, and this is exactly the category supplied by the refinement-category lemma.

Given two compactifications c₁ and c₂, form the fibre product of their ambient schemes over Y and the graph a=(j₁,j₂):X→ ar X₁×_Y ar X₂. The product is proper over Y by stability of proper morphisms under base change and composition; the graph is a quasi-compact immersion (closed graph followed by a base-changed quasi-compact open immersion). Apply the immersion-compactification construction to a. Its scheme-theoretic image gives a compactification, and its two restricted projections are proper refinements by the proper-to-separated-target lemma. Thus every pair has a common refinement.

For parallel refinements u,v:c₁→c₂, take the pullback of the diagonal of the separated proper target \bar X₂→Y along (u,v). The resulting E→\bar X₁ is a closed immersion by closed-immersion base change, hence proper; and E→Y is proper by composing it with the proper structure map \bar X₁→Y. Since uj₁=vj₁, j₁ factors uniquely through E. The pullback square is cartesian because the closed immersion E→\bar X₁ is a monomorphism: any map to E whose composite with E→\bar X₁ equals j₁ is the unique factor j_E. Thus j_E is the base change of the quasi-compact open immersion j₁, hence is a quasi-compact open immersion. Therefore E→Y is a compactification and E→\bar X₁ is a proper refinement equalizing u and v.

Nonemptiness is part of the hypothesis (a compactification is supplied). Together with the common-refinement and equalizer constructions, the defining criterion for a cofiltered category gives that the compactification category is cofiltered.

For any g:Y′→Y, base change every compactification and refinement. The base-change compactification lemma and stability of proper and open immersions show that objects remain compactifications; fibre-product uniqueness gives preservation of identities, compositions, common refinements, and equalizers. Hence base change is a functor between the two compactification categories.

For the graph common refinement a and its base change a′, the ambient base change of the scheme-theoretic image is a closed subscheme of the ambient scheme of the image of a′: apply the universal property of scheme-theoretic image to the factorization of a′ through the pulled-back closed image. The induced closed immersion is proper and lies over both projections, so it is a refinement of common refinements.

noncomputable def baseChangeFunctor (t : T ⟶ S) :
    Compactification f ⥤ Compactification (pullback.snd f t)
lean.note: Existing declarations jointly cover the item. Cofiltered.lean:81 is arbitrary-base already, requiring only QuasiCompact f and HasCompactification f; finite type supplies the former. CategoryBaseChange.lean:111 gives the specified fibre-product base-change functor, including identities, composition, common refinements and equalizing refinements. Defs.lean quasiCompact_openImmersion_iff identifies its objects with the node's quasi-compact-open compactifications under QuasiCompact f. No qcqs assumption on the base, density condition, or replacement notion is used.
